title: Curate historical docs and supersede stale plans
description:
Problem: MemorySmith has useful historical reviews and plans, but older files can still surface in search with stale claims about inactive projects, older test counts, xUnit, or aspirational semantic-search architecture. The misspelled MemorySmith.Core/Docs/Plans/SemantingSearch.md file is a concrete example: it mixes current ONNX fallback notes with future FAISS/HNSW architecture and is harder to discover by name.

Desired outcome: historical documents remain preserved, but agents can quickly tell whether a document is current, historical, superseded, or aspirational.

Scope:
- In scope: add supersession/front-matter or prominent status notes to stale reviews/plans, create or update an index that points to current source-of-truth pages, decide whether to rename or alias SemantingSearch.md, and add validation/search guidance so agents prefer current pages and memories.
- Out of scope: rewriting every historical review from scratch or deleting historical evidence.

Acceptance criteria:
- Historical review/plan files that commonly appear in search have a visible status marker.
- Current source-of-truth docs are linked from stale/high-traffic historical files.
- The semantic search plan filename typo is either corrected with a compatibility pointer or explicitly documented.
- Wiki/search guidance explains how agents should treat historical reviews versus current-state memories/pages.

Validation:
- Search for Worker, Dashboard, xUnit, SemantingSearch, FAISS, and historical validation counts after updates and confirm current status markers are visible.
- Run ./Scripts/Test-PageLinks.ps1, ./Scripts/Test-PagePathLiterals.ps1, and memory JSON parse checks.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created during 2026-05-25 deepdive audit. Evidence: MemorySmith.Core/Docs/Plans/SemantingSearch.md has a misspelled filename and mixes current ONNX/fallback notes with future FAISS/HNSW planning; older Reviews/Plans files are explicitly called historical in repository instructions but do not all carry visible supersession markers.
